name: Materials, Spares & Inventory Management
appCourse: AN APP COURSE (plan section 5): the Suite app is the Materials & Spares Planner (Suite #740, merged ce912b35b; route /dashboard/apps/midstream-downstream/materials-spares-planner, Suite module Midstream & Downstream; its tile migrations are HELD for the owner). The course names the Suite app on its learning page and in its lessons, and the course's own calculator panels (materials-register-calculator, materials-stock-calculator, materials-spares-calculator) carry every practical over the same vendored engine engines/supplychain/inventory.js for a learner without a Suite seat. Lead decisions (cat-brief): the same published fee and the same Associate/Professional/Expert certificate ladder as the other courses; prerequisite null. OPEN (reported to the lead): the Expert certificate's Suite bridge code snapshots academy_apps.module ('supply_chain'), which matches no Suite module slug, so it cannot be redeemed against the Planner until the bridge maps a course to its Suite module (see openItems).
goldensNote: EMPTY BY DECISION, as EC11, EC10, EC9, EC8, SC2, EC7 and D5. The vendored golden test-data/supplychain/goldens/inventory_cases.json carries oracle output beside its inputs. The digest reads its INPUTS only and prints the engine's own figures (and asserts every refusal message equals the golden's); naming the golden here would let numsweep resolve a lesson literal against an oracle figure the digest never prints.
enginesVendoredAt: inventory.js vendored sha-identical from petrolord-engines 110f0a0 (engines PRs #281 and #283) at its CANONICAL path by vendor_materials.sh, with its jest suite, golden, the ekene-materials fixture and README, the fixture writer, the oracle, the timing script, the negative control and FINDINGS-inventory.md: 10 new paths ledgered in VENDOR.json as kind extra, group sc3-materials-course; pin 54cf7c4 unchanged. Its runtime imports (engines/hse/safetyStats.js, lib/stats/stats.js, lib/conventions/percentile.js) were ALREADY vendored in NextGen at the 110f0a0 blobs, so nothing shared moved (four proofs a path). The suite passes 216 of 216 on NextGen's copies.

history.position: THIS COURSE TEACHES NO REPAIR HISTORY. The lead's decisions on the engine (all seven FINDINGS defaults accepted; MIT OpenCourseWare cited by lecture and slide and never reproduced; the two printed Caplice slips taught as slips with the rule's figure beside the print; the one-for-one insurance-spares model stated plainly as the engine's model with its MIL-HDBK-338B anchor) landed before any lesson was written; that is provenance.

regulatoryRule: Every text is named with its edition or date, its licence and the date read (2026-09-27), printed in digest section 2; quote_check.py pins every source file's sha256 prefix and cross-checks each against FINDINGS-inventory.md. Public-domain texts (Harris 1913, the 1913 words only; MIL-HDBK-338B) are quoted with citation, each quotation in concepts.json and verified against its text. The MIT OpenCourseWare lectures of ESD.260J (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the course is sold) are cited by lecture and slide for their figures only and never reproduced: quote_check.py checks each cited figure in the lecture text, and gate_no_ocw_prose.py refuses any eight-word run of the lecture text anywhere a learner reads. SPE-PRMS 2018 is named only, because the P-label sentence lib/conventions/percentile.js returns ends by naming it. No legal or regulatory figure: every cost, rate, service level, band, cut-off and rounding rule is a stated input.

openReadings.twelve significant digits: two figures that agree to 12 significant digits tie. Never graded: every field bit-identical under reading_exact_comparison.
openReadings.halves upward: the nearest multiple takes halves upward. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_nearest_halves_down.
openReadings.class minimum: met at or above it. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_class_minimum_exclusive.
openReadings.discount tie: the smaller quantity. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_discount_tie_larger.
openReadings.Poisson cycle-service target: met at or above it. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_poisson_target_exclusive.
openReadings.Poisson fill-rate target: met at or below the units short it allows. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_poisson_fill_exclusive.
openReadings.ABC tie: ranked by id ascending. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_abc_ties_by_id_descending.
openReadings.spares tie: fewer spares. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_spares_tie_more.
openReadings.slow-moving band minimum: reached at or above it. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_band_minimum_exclusive.
openReadings.cover limit: excess strictly above it. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_cover_limit_inclusive.
openReadings.stockout at equality: a lead-time demand equal to the reorder point is met. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_stockout_at_equality.
openReadings.reorder point for a service level: the sorted draw at ceil(level x n) - 1. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_service_index_one_high.
openReadings.Monte Carlo P90: the low figure (lib/conventions/percentile.js). Never graded: bit-identical under reading_p90_as_high, and on a second seed and draw count.

namingCollisions.service level: always names its measure: the cycle service level or the fill rate.
namingCollisions.safety stock: k times sigma over the protection period; the reorder point and the order-up-to level are named as such.
namingCollisions.EOQ: the unrounded square-root figure; the quantity ordered is the rounded one.
namingCollisions.criticality class: the class of the stated criticality policy (V, E, D in the Ekene policy), a different thing from the ABC class.
namingCollisions.P90: of a sampled lead time or demand, the low figure.
namingCollisions.obsolete, slow and excess: always of a stated band or cover limit.
namingCollisions.insurance spare: always of the stated one-for-one model.

openItems.SUITE BRIDGE CODE (for the lead; touches: The Expert certificate's Suite discount code snapshots academy_apps.module (NextGen trigger academy_expert_bridge(), migrations/20260715_ng7_advanced_tiers.sql L62-75), so a materials code carries suite_module 'supply_chain'. The Suite's generate-quote edge function matches an app on its display module name (supabase/functions/generate-quote/index.ts L290, 'Midstream & Downstream') and a module on its slug (L331, 'midstream-downstream'); 'supply_chain' matches neither, so the code cannot discount the Materials & Spares Planner (D5 appliedai's 'data_ai' against the Suite's 'data-ai' has the same fault; procurement's 'supply_chain' code has no Suite app at all). Smallest correct fix, two parts: (1) Suite generate-quote/index.ts L290 compares moduleSlugById[app.module_id] (already built at L234-238) instead of app.module, matching QuoteBuilder.jsx and L331; (2) a NextGen migration adding a nullable academy_apps.suite_module, academy_expert_bridge() inserting coalesce(suite_module, module), and suite_module 'midstream-downstream' for materials (and 'data-ai' for the data_ai apps, with unredeemed data_ai codes backfilled). Until then the learning page makes no claim about which Suite apps the code discounts.
openItems.THE P-LABEL SENTENCE: leadTimeRisk returns lib/conventions/percentile.js's EXCEEDANCE_DEFINITION, 'P90 means a 90% probability the actual quantity meets or exceeds this value, per SPE PRMS.'. The digest quotes it verbatim as the engine's words (Monte Carlo section), reads it for a lead time and a demand (P90 the low figure, the stockout risk at the P10 end, in the engine's own basis words), names SPE-PRMS 2018 in the sources table with its edition, licence and read date (read for the prms course, used here for its name only, never quoted), and pins the sentence to percentile.js in digest_prose.rules.mjs so a change upstream turns the prose gate red. No lesson may write the sentence as its own words.
openItems.APP NAMES AND THE HOME CATALOGUE: src/lib/appNames.js and src/lib/homeCatalog.js are NOT registered at the foundation: appNames.test.js requires every APP_NAMES slug to have an academy_apps row in migrations/, which the course migration (gen_course.py --migration, the ship phase) writes. They go in with the migrations. The panel registry, the learning page and its route (/dashboard/apps/materials) are registered.
openItems.READINGS COUNT: The design both earlier agents reached named eleven stated readings; the engine states thirteen (twelve significant digits, halves upward, the class minimum, the discount tie, the Poisson cycle-service target, the Poisson fill-rate target, the ABC tie, the spares tie, the band minimum, the cover limit, the stockout at equality, the service index, the Monte Carlo P90), and every field is proved bit-identical under all thirteen and on a second seed and draw count.
